`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Several "scope limits" in the draft are really impossibility results. A fixed badly approximable (BA) angle has a lower bound √(2πc) on the shortest vector of every limit lattice, and no Fermat spiral is a dense forest. Calling an unavoidable restriction a "limitation" undersells a theorem that is already in its best possible form.
- Forest and density use the same mechanism: sort a lattice-like set by norm, and a lattice-count error of o(R^{d−1}) makes the radial correction vanish. Their priority risk is one shared bet, not two separate ones.
- Contradicting an expert's published conjecture is the cheapest strong sign of significance available. It is only as good as the verbatim quote behind it.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- An explicit open question, a short classical proof, and no settling source in a limited search together support "specialist answers". They do not support "major" or "first". The bottom line is most useful when it names which results clear that bar and why.
- Most of the calibration value here came from two distinctions: "impossible" versus "not proved" (the unavoidable quantifiers), and "quoted" versus "paraphrased" (the 2022 conjecture).
